). The UK, for the first time, successfully intercepted a Russian Shadow Fleet vessel in the English Channel (14 June 2026)

as of October 2026, the UK has specified over 650 vessels under the Russia sanctions regime, including over 600 oil tankers

UK, US and EU sanctions have denied Russia access to almost $500 billion since February 2022.

between October 2024 and September 2025, UK imports from and exports to Russia of all goods dropped by 98.1% and 97.5% compared to 2021

this government has imposed sanctions against:

38 individuals and entities including Russian oil companies, shadow fleet tankers, and those supplying goods critical to Russia’s military (8 October 2026)

31 individuals and entities including LNG shadow fleet vessels, Kremlin disinformation networks and perpetrators of civilian torture and child indoctrination (1 October 2026)

19 individuals and entities enabling Russia’s war in Ukraine, further constraining the networks and revenue streams on which the Kremlin relies (6 August 2026)

24 individuals and entities behind destructive cyber and hybrid operations (13 July 2026). This is the first joint sanctions package with the EU

nearly 300 targets, including critical energy revenues and military equipment suppliers. This is the largest Russia sanctions package since the early months of 2022 (24 February 2026)

War crimes and justice

the UK has provided £22.8 million to support Ukraine’s domestic war crimes investigations

with our EU and US partners, we established the Atrocity Crimes Advisory Group to coordinate our collective technical assistance and capacity building support for Ukraine’s efforts to document, investigate and prosecute atrocity crimes

we have committed more than £4 million to support Ukrainian efforts to facilitate the return and reintegration of children forcibly deported by Russia, including a pilot tracing mechanism which has identified over 20,000 additional children since the beginning of September

we supported the resolution establishing the Operating Model of the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression which was adopted on 15 May, paving the way to hold those responsible for Russia’s war to account

we are a founding member of the Register of Damage for Ukraine, which allows Ukrainians to record losses, injury or damage as a result of the war and open for all 43 claims categories (30 September 2026)

we signed the Council of Europe Convention on the Establishment of an International Claims Commission for Ukraine (16 December 2025)

Trade

the UK-Ukraine Digital Trade Agreement has entered into force, facilitating duty-free digital content trade (1 September 2024)

the UK-Ukraine TechBridge delivers projects in mutual trade, investment, innovation research and digital skills development

the UK’s first dedicated business centre for industry in Ukraine has now opened, offering UK companies a permanent presence in Kyiv to deepen industrial ties with Ukraine (8 October 2026)

our City-Ukraine Hub leverages UK expertise to deliver capacity building projects

our provision of military equipment to deter attacks and insurance through the UK-developed Unity facility has supported the Black Sea maritime corridor and enabled Ukraine to keep exporting its goods. Ukraine exported all of its 2023 and 2024 harvests – crucial for global food security and Ukraine’s economy

the Ukraine Reconstruction Project Development Programme is a pilot programme set up by DBT to fund feasibility and scoping studies by British businesses for major reconstruction projects (1 July 2026)

UK-Ukraine Political, Free Trade and Strategic Partnership Agreement enables UK businesses to benefit from tariff free trade on all goods until 31 March 2029 (tariffs on eggs and poultry extended until 31 March 2028) (19 January 2026)

For further information visit the Department for Business and Trade’s Ukraine page.

Ukrainians in the UK

237,200 Ukrainians have arrived in the UK, including 177,600 through Homes for Ukraine (as of 31 March 2026)

the Ukraine Permission Extension (UPE) scheme opened on 4 February 2025 providing an additional 18 months permission and a continuation of the same rights and entitlements for Ukrainians in the UK on the Ukraine schemes. 147,186 UPE applications have been granted (as of 31 March 2026)

the Government recently extended the UPE scheme by an additional 24 months. This means individuals coming to the end of their initial 18 months’ permission under UPE can apply for a further 24 months under the scheme, totalling 3.5 years under UPE

the application window for UPE applications has also increased from 28-days to 90-days before an applicant’s current permission expires

English language and employment support is being provided by the UK government-funded STEP programme, a free, 12 or 24 weeks virtual programme open to all Ukrainians living in the UK on one of the humanitarian UK visa schemes

Culture

the UK has contributed over £2.5 million for the protection of Ukrainian cultural heritage across various projects. These include 2 donations to the Ukrainian Cultural Heritage Fund (UCHF), as well as donations of emergency conservation materials to Ukrainian museums

New Ukrainian GCSE to help young Ukrainians preserve their heritage while opening pathways to future education and employment for all pupils [4 Nov 2026]

the Government has supplied funding for the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE)-led Heritage Crime Task Force in Ukraine

the Government has funded Historic England for a programme to provide cultural heritage professionals with support as they work to ensure heritage is protected, preserved, and restored
